case_number: Civil Appeal No. 4134 of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (Civil) No. 2946 of 2020)
summary: The appeal involves employees of the Bhavnagar Municipal Corporation challenging the High Court's partial allowance of their claim for higher pay-scale benefits under a government scheme. The High Court limited entitlement to the higher pay-scale of Rs.5,000–8,000/- from July 31, 2018, due to delay and laches, rejecting claims for arrears from 2010. The appellants were initially granted enhanced pay based on the next promotional post but had benefits withdrawn in 2010 when the Corporation corrected what it deemed an erroneous application of the Scheme, revising pay to the next hierarchical stage (Rs.4,500–7,000/-) and recovering excess payments. The appellants filed writ petitions in 2017 relying on a prior favorable judgment in Mukeshbhai Jaswantrai Joshi's case interpreting the Scheme to allow higher promotional pay-scales. The Court considered principles of delay and laches, noting that while limitation does not strictly apply to writ petitions, equitable doctrines may be invoked. It also examined the doctrine of continuing cause of action in salary disputes, referencing case law holding that each month’s underpayment constitutes a fresh cause of action. However, recovery of arrears remains subject to time-bar defenses.
legal_provisions_cited: Scheme of Higher Grade Scale dated 16th August 1994 (Government Resolution No. PAY-1194/(44)/M)
Moons Mills Ltd. v. M.R. Mehar, President, Industrial Court, Bombay and Others, AIR 1967 SC 1450
Nav Rattanmal and Others v. State of Rajasthan, AIR 1961 SC 1704
State of Kerala and Others v. V. R. Kalliyanikutty and Another, (1999) 3 SCC 657
M.R. Gupta v. Union of India and Others, (1995) 5 SCC 628
Union of India and Others v. Tarsem Singh
Shiv Dass v. Union of India and Others
final_judgment: The appeals were allowed in part; the respondents were directed to grant the higher pay-scale benefits from the date of the Single Judge's order (31 July 2018) but not from 2010, upholding the High Court’s application of delay and laches to deny earlier arrears, while affirming the entitlement to future correct pay under the Scheme.
